rounds.title: Round 1 · truth fixes
rounds.note: Same model (GPT-6 Luna, medium effort), same picture, and the same instructions except one sentence about drawings the solver cannot solve, which none of these ten is. Four of the ten sheets are word-for-word identical between the versions, so those pairs show how much the model varies on its own.

rounds.title: Round 2 · v4: link jobs, family check, schematic filmstrip
rounds.note: Same model and effort. v4 changes the fact sheet a lot and the prompt a little (see Results), so every sheet differs. Both sides are each version's first asking; v4 was asked twice, and the second asking differs in places (the Four-Bar's second asking names wipers, the Wiper's names no uses).

Hood_Hinge.why: v4 says it is a Stephenson six-bar that resembles a car hood hinge and names car hood hinges as the use, in both askings; v3 calls it a triple-rocker four-bar and suggests windshield wiper linkages.

Cylinder_Boom.why: v4's first asking puts no part name in bold, so the panel cannot point at any part (its second asking does); v3 reads as well and names excavator booms.

Radial_Engine.why: v5 says a five-cylinder radial engine in both askings; v4f calls it a five-slider slider-crank assembly and names no use.

Oscillating_Fan.why: v5 recognizes an oscillating fan and names pedestal and table fans (its second asking missed it); v4f names windshield wipers.

Twelve library templates (eight never used), eight student mechanisms and one test case. Both sides are each version's first blind asking; both were asked five times blind, and five times with the old file names, to measure the difference.

It shows the background image at full strength and sends only mechanisms PMKS+ can solve. Round 5's twelve templates, the ten library templates never used (teaching chains with no machine behind most of them), every student mechanism that solves, and two wheel cases. Both sides are each version's first asking; both were asked five times.

rounds.title: Round 8 · the same v8 sheets, GPT-6 Astra against Claude Opus 5.5
rounds.note: The two strongest models on the same blind v8 sheets and pictures, medium effort. Over two askings both name the real machine in 18 of 22 library askings; Astra is wrong in 2 of its 20 "Looks like" lines and Opus in 4 of 22. Both take about 15 s. Opus writes longer (median 84 words to 74, five times over the 90 asked) and more specifically ("an 0-6-0 switcher's three coupled drivers"), and more often gives a real use for a teaching chain that has none. The panels apply the "Looks like" gate. Both sides are each model's first asking.

rounds.title: Round 9 · the same v8 sheets, Claude Opus 5.5 against Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
rounds.note: The strongest model against the cheapest, on the same blind v8 sheets and pictures. Over two askings Flash-Lite names the real machine in 17 of 21 library askings to Opus's 18 of 22, in about 2 s to 15 s, but it gives the same generic use ("packaging machinery") over and over, drops the bold part names four times, repeats the family PMKS+ matched, and wrote invalid JSON in 4 of 87 replies. (Its instructions reach it as a system instruction, as in the first model comparison, rather than in the message.) The panels apply the "Looks like" gate. Both sides are each model's first asking.
